RUST-03-typed-errors-evidence/README.md.content:
# Typed Records, Absence and Error Paths

This project implements the course's `A:17` parsing case. The starter is a
working numeric-status baseline. The reference replaces those conventions with
`Record`, `ParseError`, `Result`, `Option` and indexed `RowError` values. Both
roles define the same command-line behavior. Equal output does not establish
that an internal API expresses absence and failure in types.

## Grammar and error order

A record is exactly uppercase `A`, one colon, and one or more ASCII decimal
digits. Its numeric value is in `0..=65535`. Leading zeros are valid, including
representations longer than five digits when the numeric value still fits.
Spaces, signs, non-ASCII digits, extra colons and trailing characters are not
accepted. No trimming or normalization happens before validation.

Checks run in this order:

| Condition | Target error | Caller action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No colon | `MissingSeparator` | `add-separator` |
| Kind is not exactly `A` | `UnknownKind` | `choose-A` |
| Value text is empty | `MissingValue` | `supply-value` |
| Any value byte is not an ASCII digit | `InvalidNumber` | `use-ASCII-digits` |
| Decimal value does not fit `u16` | `ValueOutOfRange` | `use-u16-range` |

For example, `B:` is an unknown kind before its empty value is considered.
`A:65536x` has invalid number syntax before numeric range is considered.
`A:17:2` is an invalid number. A single empty input is missing a separator.
Every malformed case returns a value to its caller; production library logic
contains no panic, `unwrap`, `expect`, process exit, file I/O or network access.

The starter uses `-1` through `-5` for those five errors and nonnegative values
for successful parsing. Its first-record API uses `usize::MAX` as an absence
marker. These are conventions that callers must remember. The target parser
returns `Result<Record, ParseError>`. A successful `Record` has kind `Alpha` and
a `u16` value. An error has a specific variant rather than a magic number.

## Absence, context and propagation

`first_record` examines the first nonempty row. Exactly empty strings are
skipped; whitespace-only strings are not. No candidate is `Ok(None)` in the
target API, which is different from `Ok(Some(record))` containing numeric zero.
An invalid first candidate returns its error even if a later row is valid.
After a valid first candidate, later rows are outside this API's selected scope.

`RowError` retains a zero-based row index and the typed parse error. The
reference converts a missing separator from `Option` with `ok_or`, converts a
parse error into row context with `map_err`, and propagates failures with `?`.
`?` does not panic or decide the caller's action. The surrounding return type
and explicit error conversion control what can propagate.

The caller-facing display names the error class without repeating the input.
The internal row index remains available to an authorized caller. Neither
`Display` nor `Debug` needs to contain the submitted record text.

The optional `all_records` API examines every nonempty row. The reference
collects successful records and indexed errors in order rather than returning
early on the first error. This deliberately differs from `first_record`.

## Build and run

Use Rust 1.97.1, Cargo, rustfmt and Clippy. Both crates declare edition 2024 and
have no third-party dependencies. From the selected role folder:

```sh
rustc -Vv
cargo -V
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy --locked --offline --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --locked --offline
cargo run --locked --offline
cargo run --locked --offline -- --record 'A:65535'
cargo run --locked --offline -- --record 'A:65536'
cargo run --locked --offline -- --scan '' 'A:0'
cargo run --locked --offline -- --scan '' ''
cargo run --locked --offline -- --scan '' 'B:17' 'A:17'
cargo clean
cargo test --locked --offline
cargo run --locked --offline
```

The default program prints `record=Alpha value=17` and a newline, with empty
stderr and status 0. The scan containing `A:0` prints `record=Alpha value=0`;
the all-empty scan prints `record=absent`. Those are distinct successful outcomes.
The out-of-range run has empty stdout, status 65 and this stderr:

```text
error=value-out-of-range action=use-u16-range
```

The scan accepts at most eight row arguments. Unsupported command shapes and
non-UTF-8 arguments use status 64 with a static message. Only the CLI selects
exit status. The parser library returns typed values without terminating a
process. These examples use bounded supplied text fixtures; the parser does
not establish application-wide input, memory, time or authorization limits.

## Core project: replace numeric status conventions

Complete CORE, ERROR TABLE, PREDICT, CHECKS and LIMITS in `observations.md`.
Refactor the starter parser into the target `RecordKind`, `Record` and five
`ParseError` variants. Remove integer failure flags from the parser API.
Keep the exact grammar, check order, range and public CLI outcomes. Give each
error one explicit caller action. Test every variant, both range boundaries,
leading zeros, extra/trailing text and fake input whose text cannot appear in
a public error. No malformed fixture can panic.

The two roles have eight named tests, including all 65,536 representable `u16`
values. Adapt API-shaped assertions when their return types change; preserve
the underlying behavior being checked. Passing the starter tests does not
complete the typed API refactor.

## Required continuation: absence and indexed failures

Continue the same saved project and complete ABSENCE. Replace the tuple absence
marker with `Result<Option<Record>, RowError>`. Keep valid zero, no candidate
and invalid candidate separate. Preserve the first nonempty row's index,
demonstrate `ok_or` and `map_err`, and explain the two `?` propagation sites.
Record why a later valid row cannot silently erase an earlier selected error.

## Choice: collect every candidate

Complete CHOICE. Refactor `all_records` into a collection of typed successes and
indexed failures. Add a named mixed-row test using a different order from the
baseline and show that rows after an error are still examined. Explain when a
caller needs all outcomes rather than the first selected candidate.

## Challenge: type boundaries and error-display regression

Complete CHALLENGE. Predict the three standalone compile refusals, run them,
and compare the paired fixes. Add new malformed cases to test grammar priority
and prove that a fake record marker never appears in public error text.

Cargo tests cover the crate sources. Compile these independent diagnostic
files separately from the selected role directory:

```sh
mkdir -p evidence
rustfmt --edition 2024 --check diagnostics/*.rs
rustc --edition=2024 --emit=metadata diagnostics/missing-match.rs -o evidence/match.rmeta
rustc --edition=2024 --emit=metadata diagnostics/option-question-mark.rs -o evidence/option.rmeta
rustc --edition=2024 --emit=metadata diagnostics/sentinel-result.rs -o evidence/sentinel.rmeta
rustc --edition=2024 diagnostics/exhaustive-match.rs -o evidence/match
./evidence/match
rustc --edition=2024 diagnostics/option-to-result.rs -o evidence/option
./evidence/option
rustc --edition=2024 diagnostics/typed-result.rs -o evidence/typed
./evidence/typed
```

The refusals are E0004 for a missing enum arm, E0277 for using an `Option`
residual directly in a `Result` function, and E0308 for returning an integer
where a `Result` is required. The fixes exhaust the match, convert absence to
a deliberate error, and return a typed `Err`. A rejected source has no runtime
result. Exhaustive types cannot by themselves prove grammar correctness.

Keep changed source, worksheet, exact commands, tool versions and actual
stdout/stderr/status results together. Compare the reference after the independent
attempt. The historical course example's process abort is a defect to remove,
not behavior to reproduce in this runnable baseline.

References: [recoverable errors](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch09-02-recoverable-errors-with-result.html),
[Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/result/), [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/option/).

RUST-03-typed-errors-evidence/solution/o.content:
# Typed error reference observations

## CORE
The parser returns Result<Record, ParseError>, with an Alpha kind and a u16
success value. Its failure path contains a variant, never a numeric sentinel.
The CLI alone maps a typed error to its stable public code/action and status65.
The starter's corresponding integer flags are conventions to replace.

## ERROR TABLE
MissingSeparator/add-separator precedes UnknownKind/choose-A, then
MissingValue/supply-value, InvalidNumber/use-ASCII-digits and
ValueOutOfRange/use-u16-range. B: is UnknownKind. A:65536x is InvalidNumber.
Extra colons, trailing whitespace, signs and non-ASCII digits are rejected.

## PREDICT
Default is record=Alpha value=17. A:65535 succeeds; A:65536 has no stdout,
status65 and the value-out-of-range/use-u16-range stderr line. Leading zeros
are accepted according to numeric value. Empty scan is record=absent, status0;
the scan containing A:0 is record=Alpha value=0, status0. A first B:17 rejects
even if A:17 appears later. None of these public errors repeats the input text.

## CHECKS
Record actual tool versions, commands, eight test names and clean-build
results. The u16 round-trip test covers all 65,536 valid numeric values;
separate negative tests are still needed for invalid grammar and overflow.

## LIMITS
Result makes success/failure explicit and Option represents absence. These
types do not validate external grammar automatically. Exhaustive matches catch
unhandled enum variants; a catch-all arm can hide a newly added case. The lab
does not establish application authorization or global input/resource bounds.

## ABSENCE
first_record chooses the first nonempty row. It uses Ok(None) for no candidate
and Ok(Some(record)) for a valid zero or other value. RowError retains the
zero-based index and typed cause. ok_or turns missing separator into a deliberate
error; parse_value's ? propagates that error class. map_err adds the row index,
then ? propagates RowError. A later valid row does not erase the selected error.

## CHOICE
all_records maps every nonempty row to Result<Record, RowError> and collects
the outcomes in input order. It does not use ? to return from the outer
collection on the first failure. The reference includes the typed function
and one mixed-row test; the new independent order still needs a recorded test.

## CHALLENGE
The missing-match example omits ValueOutOfRange and is refused with E0004.
Option's residual cannot propagate directly from the Result-returning example
(E0277); ok_or assigns a deliberate error before ?. A numeric sentinel is
not a Result (E0308); typed Err is the matching return contract. The paired
fixes print five error codes, Err("missing-kind"), and Err("missing-value").
Record the actual diagnostics and added regression results independently.

.github/workflows/rust-typed-errors.yml.content:
name: Rust typed-errors evidence

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "RUST-03-typed-errors-evidence/**"
      - "test/verify_rust_typed_errors.py"
      - ".github/workflows/rust-typed-errors.yml"
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "RUST-03-typed-errors-evidence/**"
      - "test/verify_rust_typed_errors.py"
      - ".github/workflows/rust-typed-errors.yml"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    env:
      RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: "1.97.1"
      SOURCE_REVISION: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Install the recorded course toolchain
        run: rustup toolchain install 1.97.1 --profile minimal --component rustfmt --component clippy
      - name: Verify numeric baseline, typed target and compiler refusals
        run: python3 test/verify_rust_typed_errors.py --proof output/rust-typed-errors/proof.json
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a
        if: always()
        with:
          name: rust-typed-errors-evidence
          path: output/rust-typed-errors/
          include-hidden-files: true
          if-no-files-found: error

test/verify_rust_typed_errors.py.content:
"""Validate the complete RSS3 numeric and typed roles and intentional compiler refusals."""
import argparse
import datetime
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import signal
import subprocess
import tempfile
import tomllib

ROOT=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
PACK=ROOT/'RUST-03-typed-errors-evidence'
parser=argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
parser.add_argument('--proof',type=Path,required=True)
args=parser.parse_args();args.proof=args.proof.resolve()
assert not args.proof.exists()
assert os.getuid()!=0 and os.uname().sysname=='Linux' and os.uname().machine=='x86_64'
OUT=args.proof.parent;OUT.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
commands=[]

def sha(raw):return hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
def stop(signum,_frame):raise SystemExit(128+signum)
signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM,stop);signal.signal(signal.SIGINT,stop)

def run(command,cwd,label,expected=0,env=None):
    entry=dict(parentTaskId='rust-typed-errors-evidence',parentPid=os.getpid(),command=[os.fsdecode(value) for value in command],cwd=str(cwd),
               startTime=datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC).isoformat(),timeoutSeconds=120)
    child=subprocess.Popen(command,cwd=cwd,env=env,stdout=subprocess.PIPE,stderr=subprocess.PIPE,start_new_session=True)
    entry['pid']=child.pid
    with (OUT/'processes.jsonl').open('a') as stream:stream.write(json.dumps(dict(entry,event='start'))+'\n')
    stdout,stderr=b'',b'';cleanup='owned process exited'
    try:stdout,stderr=child.communicate(timeout=120)
    except BaseException:
        if child.poll() is None:
            os.killpg(child.pid,signal.SIGTERM)
            try:stdout,stderr=child.communicate(timeout=3)
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                os.killpg(child.pid,signal.SIGKILL);stdout,stderr=child.communicate()
        cleanup='owned process group terminated and reaped';raise
    finally:
        with (OUT/'processes.jsonl').open('a') as stream:
            stream.write(json.dumps(dict(entry,event='end',endTime=datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC).isoformat(),exitCode=child.returncode,childProcessGroupCleanup=cleanup))+'\n')
        (OUT/(label+'.stdout.txt')).write_bytes(stdout);(OUT/(label+'.stderr.txt')).write_bytes(stderr)
    assert child.returncode==expected,(label,child.returncode,stderr.decode(errors='replace'))
    commands.append(dict(label=label,exitCode=child.returncode,stdoutSha256=sha(stdout),stderrSha256=sha(stderr)))
    return stdout,stderr


source_names=run(['git','ls-files','--','RUST-03-typed-errors-evidence','.github/workflows/rust-typed-errors.yml','test/verify_rust_typed_errors.py'],ROOT,'source-inventory')[0].decode().splitlines()
assert len(source_names)==len(set(source_names))==26
source={name:(ROOT/name).read_bytes() for name in source_names}
for name,raw in source.items():
    target=OUT/'source'/name;target.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True);target.write_bytes(raw)
versions={}
for name,command in [('rustc',['rustc','-Vv']),('cargo',['cargo','-V']),('rustfmt',['rustfmt','--version']),('clippy',['cargo','clippy','--version'])]:
    versions[name]=run(command,ROOT,'version-'+name)[0].decode()
assert 'release: 1.97.1\n' in versions['rustc']
records=['A:0','A:1','A:17','A:65535','A:65534','A:00017','A:00000','A:0000065535','A:000000','A:32768','A:32767','A:256']
state=0x0E220042
for index in range(30):
    state=(state*1664525+1013904223)%2**32
    value=state%65536
    records.append('A:'+str(value).zfill(1+index%8))
assert len(records)==42
bad=['','A17',':17','B:17','a:17','A:','A:-1','A:+1','A:1.0','A:١٧','A:17 ','A:17x','A:17:2','A:65536','A:99999','A:'+'9'*96,'A:PRIVATE_MARKER','\tA:17',' A:17','A: 17']
assert len(bad)==20
actions={'missing-separator':'add-separator','unknown-kind':'choose-A','missing-value':'supply-value','invalid-number':'use-ASCII-digits','value-out-of-range':'use-u16-range'}
def predict(text):
    if ':' not in text:code='missing-separator'
    else:
        kind,value=text.split(':',1)
        if kind!='A':code='unknown-kind'
        elif not value:code='missing-value'
        elif any(ch not in '0123456789' for ch in value):code='invalid-number'
        elif int(value)>65535:code='value-out-of-range'
        else:return (f'record=Alpha value={int(value)}\n'.encode(),b'',0)
    return b'',f'error={code} action={actions[code]}\n'.encode(),65
def scan_prediction(rows):
    for row in rows:
        if row:return predict(row)
    return b'record=absent\n',b'',0
roles=[]
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='rust-typed-errors-evidence-') as temporary:
    work=Path(temporary)
    for role in ['starter','solution']:
        selected=PACK/role;directory=work/role;shutil.copytree(selected,directory)
        role_out=OUT/role;role_out.mkdir()
        env={**os.environ,'CARGO_TARGET_DIR':str(work/(role+'-target')),'CARGO_TERM_COLOR':'never'}
        lock=(directory/'Cargo.lock').read_bytes()
        manifest=tomllib.loads((directory/'Cargo.toml').read_text())
        assert manifest['package']['edition']=='2024' and 'dependencies' not in manifest
        assert tomllib.loads(lock.decode())['package']==[{'name':'typed_record_lab','version':'0.1.0'}]
        run(['cargo','fmt','--all','--check'],directory,role+'-format',env=env)
        paths=sorted(str(p.relative_to(directory)) for p in (directory/'diagnostics').glob('*.rs'));assert len(paths)==6
        run(['rustfmt','--edition','2024','--check',*paths],directory,role+'-diagnostic-format',env=env)
        run(['cargo','clippy','--locked','--offline','--all-targets','--','-D','warnings'],directory,role+'-clippy',env=env)
        assert b'8 passed; 0 failed' in run(['cargo','test','--locked','--offline'],directory,role+'-tests',env=env)[0]
        run(['cargo','build','--locked','--offline'],directory,role+'-build',env=env)
        binary=Path(env['CARGO_TARGET_DIR'])/'debug/typed_record_lab'
        default=run([str(binary)],directory,role+'-default',env=env);assert default==predict('A:17')[:2]
        for index,text in enumerate(records):
            for mode in ['record','scan']:
                argv=['--record',text] if mode=='record' else ['--scan','',text]
                expected=predict(text)
                assert run([str(binary),*argv],directory,f'{role}-input-{index}-{mode}',env=env)==expected[:2]
        for index,text in enumerate(bad):
            for mode in ['record','scan']:
                argv=['--record',text] if mode=='record' else ['--scan','',text]
                expected=predict(text) if mode=='record' else scan_prediction(['',text])
                assert run([str(binary),*argv],directory,f'{role}-bad-{index}-{mode}',expected=expected[2],env=env)==expected[:2]
        for index,rows in enumerate([[],[''],['',''],['']*8]):
            assert run([str(binary),'--scan',*rows],directory,f'{role}-absence-{index}',env=env)==scan_prediction(rows)[:2]
        for name,rows in [('success-first',['A:17','B:0']),('error-first',['A:','A:17'])]:
            expected=scan_prediction(rows)
            assert run([str(binary),'--scan',*rows],directory,role+'-'+name,expected=expected[2],env=env)==expected[:2]
        for index,argv in enumerate([['--other'],['--record'],['--record','A:17','extra'],['--scan',*(['']*9)]]):
            assert run([str(binary),*argv],directory,f'{role}-usage-{index}',expected=64,env=env)==(b'',b'usage: typed_record_lab [--record record | --scan [record ...]]\n')
        for name,argv in [('invalid-record',[b'--record',b'\xff']),('invalid-mode',[b'\xff'])]:
            assert run([os.fsencode(binary),*argv],directory,role+'-'+name,expected=64,env=env)==(b'',b'arguments must be valid UTF-8\n')
        for name,code in [('missing-match','E0004'),('option-question-mark','E0277'),('sentinel-result','E0308')]:
            target=role_out/(name+'.rmeta')
            stdout,stderr=run(['rustc','--edition=2024','--emit=metadata','diagnostics/'+name+'.rs','-o',str(target)],directory,role+'-'+name,expected=1,env=env)
            assert not stdout and code.encode() in stderr and not target.exists()
        hashes={}
        for name,output in [('exhaustive-match',b'missing-separator\nunknown-kind\nmissing-value\ninvalid-number\nvalue-out-of-range\n'),('option-to-result',b'Err("missing-kind")\n'),('typed-result',b'Err("missing-value")\n')]:
            target=role_out/name
            run(['rustc','--edition=2024','diagnostics/'+name+'.rs','-o',str(target)],directory,role+'-'+name+'-build',env=env)
            assert run([str(target)],directory,role+'-'+name+'-run',env=env)==(output,b'')
            hashes[name]=sha(target.read_bytes())
        run(['cargo','clean'],directory,role+'-clean',env=env);assert not binary.exists()
        assert b'8 passed; 0 failed' in run(['cargo','test','--locked','--offline'],directory,role+'-clean-tests',env=env)[0]
        run(['cargo','build','--locked','--offline'],directory,role+'-clean-build',env=env)
        assert run([str(binary)],directory,role+'-clean-default',env=env)==default
        assert (directory/'Cargo.lock').read_bytes()==lock
        assert all(p.read_bytes()==(selected/p.relative_to(directory)).read_bytes() for p in directory.rglob('*') if p.is_file())
        shutil.copyfile(binary,role_out/'typed_record_lab')
        roles.append(dict(role=role,inputCases=84,unitTests=8,unitTestsBeforeAndAfterClean=True,sourceAndLockUnchanged=True,all65536ValuesTested=True,numericBaselineOrTypedTarget='numeric baseline' if role=='starter' else 'typed target',fixedExecutableSha256=hashes,executableSha256=sha(binary.read_bytes())))
assert not work.exists() and all((ROOT/name).read_bytes()==raw for name,raw in source.items())
assert len(commands)==315,len(commands)
proof=dict(sourceRevision=os.environ.get('SOURCE_REVISION'),sourceFiles={n:sha(r) for n,r in source.items()},compilerVersions=versions,commands=commands,roles=roles,nativeExecuted=True,ordinaryUser=True,allSourceFilesUnchanged=True,temporarySourceCleanup=True,externalDependencyDownloadsDuringChecks=False,worksheetCompletionNotInferred=True,productionResourceLimitsNotInferred=True)
args.proof.write_text(json.dumps(proof,indent=2)+'\n')
print(json.dumps(dict(sourceFiles=26,commands=len(commands),validInputCases=168,compilerRefusals=6,fixedPrograms=6,temporarySourceCleanup=True)))
